newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-MORE THAN 55 INJURED IN RUSSIA SOCCER RIOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MORE THAN 55 INJURED IN RUSSIA SOCCER RIOT.

text.p: More than 55 people were injured on Friday when 500 angry soccer fans battled with police in a town near Moscow after their team lost at home, RIA news agency and a local Moscow television station reported.

They said police in the town of Selyatino, some 50 km (35 miles) south of Moscow, fired in the air in a bid to restore order after CSKA Moscow fans went on the rampage in the wake of a 3-1 defeat by lowly Chernomorets Novorossisk.

At least 25 policemen and 30 supporters were injured, one of them critically, as fans fought police inside and outside the ground. Moscow's 2x2 television said hooligans had smashed the windows of several vehicles.
The riot was the latest in a series of violent incidents to mar soccer games in Russia, where until recently hooliganism was almost unheard of.
A spokesman for the Russian soccer union told RIA that CSKA would be fined heavily and could be thrown out of the league.
The team usually plays in Moscow but moved its match to Selyatino on the advice of police because three other major soccer matches were played in the capital the same day.
A crew for Russian national television filmed the fighting but the channel will only air the footage on Saturday, an official at the station said by telephone.
In September, Rotor Volgograd were forced to play a home game behind closed doors because fans hurled bottles and stones at Dynamo Moscow players after their side lost.
In May, Krylya Sovetov Samara were banned from playing at home for three matches after fans threw bottles and stones at visiting Spartak Moscow players and officials.
